title: Shared Mobile AR Without Depth Sensors from Monocular Point Maps
abstract: Depth-aware augmented reality on phones needs dense geometry of the surrounding room. iPhones and iPads without LiDAR expose only sparse feature points and detected planes, and ARKit often takes tens of seconds to report the first wall. We describe a scan-free pipeline for these devices. A point-map network (MoGe-2) predicts metric geometry from each camera frame, the remaining depth shift is recovered from the camera intrinsics, and each frame's scale is aligned to views already in the map. A persistent voxel map with visibility-based expiry answers occlusion and collision queries. Co-located devices share one coordinate frame by solving yaw and floor-plane translation from sightings of each other. We evaluate the deployed system on 309 device-sessions from 19 device models without LiDAR, with 179 device-sessions from LiDAR phones in the same deployment as a reference population. A first dense depth map was recorded within 10 s in 80% of sessions, while ARKit had reported a wall plane by then in 25%. title: TopSDF: Topological Signed Distance Field for High-Quality Triangle Mesh Extraction from 3D Gaussian Splatting
abstract: Recent advances in 3D Gaussian Splatting (3DGS) have demonstrated its effectiveness for photorealistic novel view synthesis. However, extracting clean, watertight, explicit surface meshes from 3DGS remains a critical challenge. Previous methods approximate geometry via discrete Marching Tetrahedra, where each grid vertex is assigned a single scalar signed distance value. At complex geometric boundaries and thin structures, this suboptimal parameterization forces severe compromises across shared vertices, causing gradient collisions and geometric frustration. Furthermore, existing optimization objectives neglect element shape conditioning, producing degenerate triangles. We introduce TopSDF, a framework that models the signed distance state as a multivariate Gaussian random field. By learning latent topological covariances across tetrahedral vertices, our formulation expands local degrees of freedom for SDF estimates, allowing the candidate mesh vertices to be placed flexibly along the bipolar edges in the tetrahedra as driven by such topological correlation. title: Is It Still There? Place-Registered Verification Makes VLMs Reliable Scene-Change Detectors
abstract: A robot that returns to a space must tell which objects were added, removed or moved since its last visit, while its trajectory, viewpoints and lighting differ between the two visits. We find that multi-image vision-language models (VLMs) fail at this task mainly because they cannot find the place where an object was. A VLM recognises what each frame shows but cannot check whether an object is still at its place in the other capture. It therefore reports objects that only one capture shows and misses most removed and moved objects. We propose STILL, which reformulates change detection as object verification at a registered place. 3D geometry registers the place of each change hypothesis in the other capture, and one VLM answers, from a scene view and a local place view, whether the object is still at that place, trained with supervision of the same form. Under the official SceneDiff protocol, STILL raises the main metric obj/sc AP from 24.0 to 37.8, and from 11.6 to 20.6 on the egocentric kitchen subset without any kitchen training data. It improves F1 by more than 21 points over a VLM fine-tuned on the same annotations and adds only about 11% to the runtime.

title: LongCat-Video-Avatar 1.6 Technical Report
abstract: Recent advances in audio-driven avatar video generation have enabled increasingly realistic synthesis, yet achieving precise lip-audio synchronization, natural, human-like motion, and visual consistency over long sequences remains challenging. We present LongCat-Video-Avatar 1.6, which builds on LongCat-Video-Avatar 1.5 to improve expressive naturalness and reduce error accumulation during extended generation, e.g., exaggerated lip movements and overly red, temporally unstable lip coloration, enhance the naturalness of facial expressions and coordinated head and body movements. These improvements are driven by a refined post-training pipeline that integrates reinforcement learning, improved classifier-free guidance strategies for DMD-based few-step distillation, long-video rollouts, and on-policy distillation. Together, these refinements improve expressive realism and enable the generation of videos exceeding 10 minutes while maintaining visual quality and temporal consistency. Arena evaluations show that LongCat-Video-Avatar 1.6 outperforms its predecessor and competing commercial audio-driven avatar models, demonstrating the effectiveness of the improved post-training pipeline.

title: CISyn: Human Mesh Recovery in Close Interactions with Physics-Simulated Synthetic Data
abstract: 3D human mesh recovery (HMR) in close-interaction scenarios is hindered by the lack of large-scale, accurately annotated training data: real capture is expensive, and existing synthetic datasets rarely include physical contact. We introduce CISyn, a large-scale synthetic dataset purpose-built for close human-human interactions, generated via physics simulation and Blender-based rendering. By simulating collision dynamics between SMPL-X-rigged humanoids, CISyn naturally produces the contact, mutual occlusion, and pose entanglement that characterize close-interaction scenes, with no manual annotation effort. The released set provides 25,000 sequences with accurate 3D annotations. We further propose an uncertainty-aware loss that allows models to learn more effectively from the heavily occluded examples in our data. Augmenting state-of-the-art HMR training with CISyn and replacing the regression loss with our uncertainty-aware variant yields consistent improvements on close-interaction benchmarks, validating CISyn as a scalable complement to real-world data. The dataset, generation pipeline, and code are available at https://github.com/yfde/CISyn.

title: Probing Where Surprise Happens: Localized Violation-of-Expectation Evaluation of Video World Models
abstract: Violation-of-expectation (VOE) benchmarks evaluate intuitive physics in video world models by testing whether physically impossible events produce greater prediction errors than matched possible events. However, conventional VOE evaluations aggregate prediction errors across space and time, making it unclear whether successful discrimination reflects model's understanding of physical violations at the locations and time where they occur. To address this limitation, we introduce localized VOE evaluation, a framework that measures prediction error differences between possible and impossible events within spatial regions and temporal intervals associated with physical violations. We compare global, temporally localized, and spatiotemporally localized evaluations of V-JEPA models pretrained on developmental egocentric videos or large-scale natural video datasets. Our results reveal that global and localized judgments can diverge in both directions: global aggregation can either obscure correct localized discrimination or produce apparent discrimination without corresponding localized evidence. title: DEFDVO: Deformable Deep Visual Odometry for Equirectangular Images
abstract: Omnidirectional ($360^\circ$) cameras capture the full surrounding scene in every frame, providing a strong advantage for visual odometry (VO) over pinhole sensors with a limited field of view. However, their equirectangular projection (ERP) introduces latitude-dependent distortion, an artificial seam at the image border, and a sampling bias toward the poles. Existing $360^\circ$ VO methods address these challenges only partially. DEFDVO closes this gap with a patch-based deep VO method that operates directly on ERP imagery, combining spherically initialized deformable feature extraction, end-to-end seam-aware estimation, and spherical-gradient patch selection. The deformable feature extractor combines spherical geometric priors with learned sampling offsets, while seam-aware processing preserves ERP continuity, and spherical-gradient selection reduces polar sampling bias. Trained exclusively on synthetic TartanAirV2 ERP imagery, DEFDVO improves the best prior average absolute trajectory error (ATE) by $4.8\times$ (0.201 m to 0.042 m) on the TartanAirV2 evaluation set defined by 360DVO and achieves the lowest average ATE on both splits of the real-world 360DVO benchmark. title: AdaptType: Accessible and Customizable Multimodal Text Entry in Virtual Reality for People with Upper-Body Motor Impairments
abstract: Text entry in virtual reality (VR) is cumbersome, especially for people with upper-body motor impairments. Existing techniques often demand both fine and gross motor control, yet users' motor abilities vary widely. To address this range of needs, we present AdaptType, a multimodal VR text entry system that enables users to configure input techniques that best suit their abilities, and scaffolds customization through ability-based recommendations. Through a study with 10 participants, we found that customized multimodal techniques improved text entry speed compared to gaze- or hand-only techniques, and complemented voice for error correction, decreasing failure rate from 15.1% to 2.0%. We found that AdaptType yielded high text entry speed (36.26 WPM) and accuracy (0.36% error rate), with low task load and high usability ratings. We also found ability-based recommendations effectively scaffolded customization. Our work contributes more accessible and personalized VR text entry solutions for people with upper-body motor impairments.

title: Prepare Lighter and Faster for Open-Vocabulary Queries: A Query-Wise 3D Segmenter for Gaussian Splatting
abstract: Open-vocabulary 3D understanding aims to localize and segment arbitrary objects beyond predefined categories. However, existing approaches based on Gaussian Splatting often rely on expensive preprocessing and lengthy training, limiting their applicability when fast and lightweight solutions are desired. We propose a lightweight, training-free framework for query-driven 3D instance segmentation on Gaussian Splatting. Instead of conventional mask-wise CLIP embeddings, we use dense pixel-level CLIP features to preserve fine-grained semantic information and enable flexible text-driven localization without relying on predefined instance proposals. Given a text query, we identify a high-quality target region in a carefully selected pivot view and propagate it across views using a video segmentor, providing consistent and comprehensive coverage of the target instance. We then lift the resulting 2D tracklets to 3D Gaussians through a novel visibility voting strategy, yielding accurate 3D segmentation masks with clean object boundaries. Extensive experiments demonstrate state-of-the-art performance on LERF-OVS, ScanNet, and ScanNet++, competitive results on 3D-OVS, and significant speedups

title: M-CROSS: A Multisensor Simulation Dataset for SLAM across Water–Land Transitions
abstract: Water--land cross-domain robots require continuous localization across land, transition and underwater phases, where sensor characteristics and availability change abruptly. Existing datasets and conventional metrics are not designed to capture transition-induced degradation and failures. We present \textbf{M-CROSS}, to the best of our knowledge, the first multisensor simulation dataset and benchmark for SLAM across continuous water--land transitions. It provides synchronized LiDAR, sonar, stereo camera, IMU, DVL, and depth measurements; 6DoF pose ground truth; sensor-wise medium-state annotations; and medium-dependent sensor degradation models. We establish a transition-aware protocol comprising the Trajectory Completion Rate (TCR), Piecewise Absolute Pose Error (PW-APE), Transition End Error (TEE), and Transition Survival Period (TSP), which measure trajectory completion, single-domain accuracy, transition-induced error, and localization survival under prolonged partial immersion, respectively. title: JEPA4R: Embodied JEPA World Models with 4D Point Planning
abstract: Joint-embedding predictive architecture (JEPA) world models predict future embeddings instead of pixels and plan in latent space. Two challenges remain: 2D images leave the metric geometry that manipulation acts on implicit and entangled with appearance, and what these models imagine stays hidden, as they are mostly judged in simulation by short-horizon latent planning. We present JEPA4R, a JEPA world model that observes single-depth-camera point clouds, predicts and plans in their latent space, and acts through a policy head on its frozen latents; we call this 4D point planning. A decoder on the frozen world model shows what it imagines as 4D point clouds, with a mean point error within 1.1 cm over 200 steps. Under the policy-learning protocols of OGBench and CortexBench, JEPA4R leads pixel JEPA models on OGBench Cube-Single, Cube-Double, Cube-Triple and Scene, and ranks first on MetaWorld and Adroit Relocate with 98.4% and 88.0%, above the runner-up, R3M, at 96.0% and 65.3%. Trained only in a digital twin, JEPA4R and its policy heads run zero-shot on the real arm with both a gripper and a dexterous hand.

title: SemLite-GS: Semantic-Selective Parallel Gaussian Splatting for Lightweight Building Reconstruction from UAV Oblique Imagery
abstract: Lightweight 3D building models support urban spatial analysis, but their production often requires dense scene reconstruction, building extraction, and mesh simplification. Although 3D Gaussian Splatting (3DGS) is more efficient than conventional multi-view stereo, existing large-scale methods lack semantic selection and parallel instance-level training. We present SemLite-GS, a building-centric framework that reconstructs lightweight building meshes from large-scale UAV oblique imagery. First, an orthographic reference map establishes globally consistent building identities, which are propagated to oblique views to form camera-instance pairs and regions of interest. Second, semantic-selective parallel PGSR training jointly processes multiple pairs within relevant image regions while updating only target Gaussians; contextual Gaussians remain fixed to preserve visibility. Third, architectural planes extracted from rendered depth, opacity, and normal maps guide signed distance field optimization, producing meshes with adaptive polygon allocation and well-defined structural boundaries. title: Pros4D: Modeling Evolving 4D Worlds in Latent Space for Dynamic Spatial Reasoning
abstract: Dynamic spatial reasoning from monocular video enables vision-language models (VLMs) to understand how 3D environments evolve over time, supporting physical world understanding and embodied intelligence. Existing efforts primarily address observed-dynamics understanding, whereas agents in dynamic environments also require future-dynamics prediction beyond the observation boundary. Moreover, external geometric processing and textual descriptions can increase inference complexity or lose information when representing continuous dynamics. These limitations motivate a shared internal state that preserves observed dynamics and remains predictive beyond the input video. Accordingly, we present Pros4D, a framework for modeling evolving 4D worlds in latent space that unifies retrospective understanding of observed-dynamics with prospective reasoning for future-dynamics prediction. Specifically, Pros4D-Engine derives geometry-grounded supervision and constructs paired examples for both tasks, while Pros4D-Bench evaluates them across eight spatial task categories spanning dynamic cameras, objects, and scenes. title: WL-Headset Law: Projecting Future Headset Evolution from a Decade of Display and Mass Data
abstract: Tracking a decade of headset display and mass changes can inform forecasts. However, comparing headset resolution requires pixels per degree (PPD), which is often unreported and estimated using unclear assumptions. Therefore, we compile the open-source, evidence-linked HMD Resolution and Mass Database (HRMD) with 241 configurations from 2016--2026 and introduce structure- and axis-aware robust calibration (SARC) to estimate missing central PPD. Compared with official PPD, SARC reduces PPD estimation error from 14.8% for traditional geometric estimation to 3.2%. Based on HRMD, we introduce the Weight-Linked Headset Law (WL-Headset Law), which models PPD by year, mass, and category. The law reveals 7.4% annual PPD growth at fixed mass and category. Meanwhile, head-worn mass fell by 6.5% annually after category adjustment. At an eyeglass-like mass of 30g, the law projects average central PPD of 60 (normal visual acuity) around 2035 and 120 (higher acuity) around 2044 if trends persist.

title: DoF-Query Transformer for Adaptive Fusion of Egocentric Vision and Forearm HD-sEMG in Continuous Hand Kinematics
abstract: Continuous and accurate estimation of human hand kinematics is important not only for intuitive human-machine interaction, but also for capturing fine-grained human manipulation demonstrations that can provide action supervision for embodied-intelligence datasets and dexterous robot learning. However, individual sensing modalities may be insufficient for reliable estimation under varying operating conditions. We present a finger-unencumbered multimodal framework for continuous regression of 20 hand joint angles from egocentric RGB images and 128-channel forearm high-density surface electromyography (HD-sEMG). The framework combines a Vision Transformer-based visual encoder, a Transformer-based EMG encoder, and a degree of freedom (DoF) query Transformer fusion decoder. To account for the varying informativeness of visual and EMG cues across joint DoFs and input conditions, the decoder assigns a separate learnable query to each DoF, enabling DoF-specific and context-adaptive fusion of the two modalities. title: From XR Sketches to CAD: Preserving Design Intent with AI
abstract: Extended reality (XR) allows designers to sketch shapes directly in 3D, but converting these sketches into editable, feature-based CAD requires interpreting their intent. A sketch may contain drawing errors, intended features, and design choices that remain open. Correcting every irregularity risks erasing intended features, while automatic completion may impose choices the designer has not made. We argue that AI should add precision without overriding design intent, considering both the resulting shape and how the CAD model behaves during later edits. To guide this process, we propose a conceptual framework that distinguishes errors from intentions in individual sketch properties and relates them to correction, preservation, and exploration in editable CAD. We also outline five research directions for sketch interpretation, CAD construction, and evaluation, with testable hypotheses for selected questions.

title: CiGS: Conduction in Gaussian Splats for Interior Temperature Field from Thermal Images
abstract: We present a method for inferring the interior temperature distribution of a solid object from registered multi-view visible-spectrum and thermal images, even when the thermal views cover only part of its surface. We formulate steady-state heat conduction as a Laplace boundary value problem and solve it with a direct boundary integral equation discretized over a point cloud: a Gaussian reconstruction of the visible-spectrum images supplies the boundary geometry, and the thermal images supply the boundary data. We do not build surface or volume meshes at any stage in our method. Instead, we sample collocation points from rendered depth without the pixels at depth discontinuities, and use a density subtraction that keeps the interior evaluation accurate up to the surface. The whole chain is differentiable, and we use it to recover the pose and depth of heating pipes, insulation defects, and the shape of cracks from thermal images. We validate our method through experiments on boundary value problems with Dirichlet-only and mixed Dirichlet and Robin boundaries, using synthetic and real captured data on scenes with challenging topology. title: RemeshingAgent: Self-Evolving Agent for Repair-Based Decimation of Generated Building Meshes
abstract: Aggressively simplifying a generated high-poly building mesh to 0.5-1% of its faces confronts a hard limit. The surface looks complete, yet the mesh is topologically shattered: 10^3-10^4 connected components and non-manifold thin walls. Below a certain budget, every practical decimator "melts": it deletes parts, welds thin walls, or breaks the error tolerance. We attribute this to instance-specific pathology: which components are significant and where the cliff sits vary from mesh to mesh, so no single fixed algorithm suffices, and decimation becomes an iterative loop of cleaning, simplifying, and verifying. We present RemeshingAgent, an agent that turns this loop into a validated process. title: A Gaussian Primitive Data Management Framework for Efficient 3DGS Trajectory Rendering
abstract: Trajectory rendering, which renders novel views of a reconstructed 3D scene along a camera path, is a core operation in digital twins and autonomous inspection. Structured 3D Gaussian Splatting (3DGS) renders a single view in real time by decoding sparse anchors into Gaussians on demand, but it renders a trajectory view by view: every view projects all anchors to select them, re-decodes anchors already requested by neighboring views, and runs all steps on the GPU while the CPU idles. We treat this as a spatial data management problem, where anchors are spatial objects, views are range queries, and decoded Gaussians are shared derived data, and propose GDM-GS, which removes redundancy at three levels. Within a view, an anchor index and an occluder index answer each view as a holed-frustum range query, so out-of-view and provably hidden anchors are never decoded. Across views, shared materialization decodes each requested anchor once per group of consecutive views while preserving each view's selection. title: √VINS-Based 360 Visual-Inertial SLAM Systems: Hilti–Trimble SLAM Challenge 2026 Entry
abstract: This report describes our submission to the 2026 Hilti-Trimble SLAM Challenge. The system is a 360-camera visual-inertial pipeline that uses only the provided dual-fisheye image streams and IMU measurements. First, raw images are preprocessed with low-light enhancement and static/dynamic masking, and then fed into a $\sqrt{\text{VINS}}$ frontend as the local odometry, with deep learning-based SuperPoint features, ELSED line segments, and LightGlue matching. The resulting trajectory is refined using a GTSAM-based backend that performs tightly-coupled factor graph optimization with SALAD global descriptor and visual bundle adjustment (BA). The backend performs local-to-global structureless BA, tightly regularized intrinsic and extrinsic refinement, and global scale adjustment supported by the known inter-camera baseline and cross-view constraints. The design targets long indoor sequences with dark regions, repetitive corridors, dynamic objects, and limited geometric parallax, while keeping the pipeline reproducible in the provided ROS2 workspace. Fig. 1 demonstrates that our proposed method aligns well with the floorplan across several indoor sequences.

title: OrthoMark: Place Recognition with Point-Anchored Orthographic Height Mark
abstract: LiDAR place recognition provides the loop closures of Simultaneous Localization and Mapping(SLAM). Perspective from Z-axis, a gravity-aligned scan is an orthographic map of the scene, and a revisit from another position and heading moves this map rigidly in the plane, a motion that a polar Fourier spectrum ignores and phase correlation recovers. Along the vertical, the heights of the returns describe the structures, but which heights are observed depends on the range, because the sensor's vertical field of view cuts nearby structures low; height thus misleads a global key, yet is decisive once two scans are aligned and compared cell by cell where they overlap. title: Correspondence-Free Camera Pose Estimation by Matching Moments
abstract: The blind perspective-$n$-point (PnP) problem is to estimate the pose of a calibrated camera from 2D and 3D point sets with unknown correspondences. We show that, for complete, noiseless observations, fourteen permutation-invariant image moments up to order four identify a fixed camera pose for almost every 3D point set containing at least twenty points. Our learning-free method, MomentPnP, matches these moments between the observed 2D points and the projected 3D points to initialize a camera pose without correspondences and refines the pose and correspondence weights using expectation--maximization. Across the test sets of three benchmarks, our method reduces median rotation error by $5$--$170\times$ relative to the best learned baseline, both with and without outliers. We recover accurate poses even with as many outliers as inliers. On dense ETH3D scans, pose accuracy improves as the point sets grow, even as individual correspondences become harder to resolve.

title: Multi-Rate Flow Matching for Point Cloud Upsampling
abstract: Flow-matching point-cloud upsamplers refine sparse inputs into dense point clouds by integrating a learned velocity field with a fixed temporal discretization. However, local reconstruction requirements vary substantially across a shape, while a shared solver budget applies the same temporal resolution everywhere. We propose Multi-Rate Flow Matching (MRFM), a patch-adaptive framework that selects an integration budget for each local patch at inference time while keeping the learned velocity field frozen. MRFM relaxes the discrete budget into a continuous variable, optimizes it online through differentiable soft rollouts using an input-derived geometric fidelity objective, and projects the result back to a discrete budget for the final solver rollout. Experiments on PU1K and PUGAN show strong reconstruction quality, while matched-budget permutation and multi-factor analyses demonstrate that the benefit depends on patch-specific allocation rather than on the step distribution alone. MRFM is accuracy-oriented and intentionally uses additional test-time optimization to obtain more suitable local temporal resolutions.

title: ROSE: A Shared Cross-Embodiment Facial-Motion Latent Space for Humanoid Robot Expression
abstract: Natural, coherent full-face dynamic expressions are central to making humanoid robots socially approachable, yet existing systems commonly realize only limited lip motion or scripted expressions. The limitation is both physical and algorithmic. A compact head leaves little room for densely packed, independently controllable actuation; meanwhile, learned systems often generate an avatar video, landmarks, or facial parameters and then infer actuator commands through visual retargeting. This render-and-invert path adds latency and artifacts, and it does not reliably transfer generated behavior to a physical robot. We present ROSE (RObot facial expression through Shared motion Embeddings), a framework that integrates biomimetic hardware, cross-embodiment motion representation learning, and multimodal motion generation. On the hardware side, we build a flexible tendon-sheath transmission structure that integrates 34 actuators into a 19.5 cm biomimetic head. By decoupling actuator placement from facial action points, it enables coordinated full-face expression within a compact volume. title: Body of Evidence: Triangulating 3D Human Pose with Geometry-Conditioned Depth
abstract: Even in multi-camera setups, occlusions can leave individual body joints with only a single usable 2D observation. Such an observation defines a viewing ray but leaves the joint's depth undetermined. We introduce Body of Evidence (BoE), a multi-view 3D human pose estimator that predicts per-camera joint depths alongside 2D joint locations. To reduce monocular depth ambiguity, we propose geometry-conditioned depth prediction, which combines image features with previously reconstructed 3D body geometry as contextual depth cues. We further introduce learnable depth-aware triangulation (LDAT), which augments differentiable algebraic triangulation with predicted depth constraints, enabling reconstruction even from a single contributing camera while preserving the benefits of geometric triangulation when multiple views are available. The reconstructed 3D poses subsequently guide depth prediction in the next iteration, allowing depth estimates and 3D geometry to progressively refine each other. title: MetricHand: Geometry-Aware Flow Matching for 4D Hand Reconstruction in Metric World Space
abstract: Egocentric hand motion provides physical motion supervision for dexterous manipulation and vision-language-action pretraining. Reliable use of this supervision requires accurate and temporally coherent 4D hand reconstruction in metric world space. Existing methods typically lift framewise estimates produced under weak perspective into world coordinates. By ignoring joint-dependent depth variation at close range, this approximation couples errors in translation, orientation, and articulation that persist after world lifting and worsen under occlusion. We present MetricHand, a geometry-aware flow matching framework for 4D hand reconstruction in metric world space. MetricHand encodes depth priors from hand-object interaction regions into joint-associated representations that preserve local spatial structure and metric scale. Fused with visual features, this geometry guides coarse metric estimation and conditions every step of temporal generation. The model jointly recovers world-space translation, global orientation, MANO articulation, and shape, while structural priors and temporal context support estimation under partial occlusion. title: WinDEX: Metric 3D Hand Motion Reconstruction in the Wild for Dexterous Teleoperation and Policy Learning
abstract: Human manipulation data are widely used to train robots for human-like dexterity. However, low-cost, large-scale collection in the wild remains challenging. Existing methods remain limited in geometrically grounded metric-scale reconstruction, real-world generalization and inference speed. We present WinDEX, integrating (1) geometric-temporal optimization for metric 3D hand annotation from in-the-wild egocentric stereo videos, combined with visual-inertial SLAM for world-frame reconstruction; (2) WinDEX-Net, an end-to-end, fisheye-native network combining calibrated stereo, local detail and temporal context, with a data-model flywheel of model-assisted annotation and retraining; (3) distilled models for offline reconstruction and causal streaming, supporting reinforcement learning and teleoperation; and (4) low-cost CyberCap stereo-inertial capture, forming the WinDEX-Hand dataset with 1,000 hours of training annotations and held-out human-annotated in-the-wild 2D and independent optical motion-capture evaluation sets. title: A Study on Performance Enhancement of a Webcam-Based Real-Time Eye-Tracking System
abstract: This study proposes a real-time gaze-tracking system that uses a standard RGB webcam to estimate screen coordinates. The system combines ETH-XGaze-based gaze estimation with nine-point calibration and polynomial ridge regression. To reduce errors caused by changes in head position, it also applies a conditional residual correction derived from head and pose features extracted with RTMPose. Whether this correction is used depends on the reliability of the detected features and the characteristics of the calibration data. In a preliminary experiment, one participant completed trials at 12 screen targets. The resulting mean screen-coordinate error was 204.24 pixels, which was 35.83% lower than that of xgaze-js and 57.69% lower than that of gaze_tracker. The system produced valid gaze estimates for all 12 targets. These preliminary findings demonstrate the feasibility of combining user-specific calibration with conditional pose-based correction for webcam gaze tracking. Because the evaluation involved only one participant, further experiments with more participants and a wider range of postures are required.

title: QuantileGS: Quantile-Based Conformal Bounds on RGB Rendering Errors for Novel View Synthesis with 3D Gaussian Splatting
abstract: Uncertainty quantification for novel view synthesis with 3D Gaussian Splatting (3DGS) assesses rendering reliability at unseen viewpoints. This reliability depends on the discrepancy between rendered and true colors, which cannot be measured without ground-truth images. We therefore quantify uncertainty in this unknown discrepancy through upper bounds on per-pixel RGB mean absolute error. However, learned bounds may underestimate these errors and overstate rendering reliability, motivating calibration to a prescribed coverage level. In this paper, we propose QuantileGS, a post-hoc framework that combines learned rendering-error quantiles with scale-normalized conformal calibration to produce spatially adaptive error bounds. The framework comprises three phases. Phase 1, Rendering-Error Computation, measures RGB mean absolute error between observed images and predictions from a frozen 3DGS model. Phase 2, Ordered Gaussian Quantile Fields, learns two scalar attributes per Gaussian to predict lower and upper rendering-error quantiles. title: Real-world Polarimetric Environment Map Dataset
abstract: Environment maps are a standard representation of illumination, enabling realistic image-based lighting in modern rendering systems. However, existing environment maps typically encode only RGB radiance, omitting polarization, an intrinsic property of light that is imperceptible to the human eye but informative about surface shape and material properties. This omission precludes the physically accurate simulation of polarized light transport under in-the-wild illumination conditions, heavily limiting the development and evaluation of robust polarization-based scene reconstruction and understanding methods. We address this gap by introducing a real-world polarimetric environment map dataset, each providing a full-sphere panorama with per-pixel high-dynamic-range RGB Stokes vectors. To acquire the dataset, we design and calibrate a dedicated imaging system and develop a polarization-aware panorama-stitching pipeline. In particular, we introduce a frame-field representation for perspective cameras, together with singularity-aware blending, to enable smooth polarimetric panorama stitching without singularity artifacts. title: The Mask Is Not the Object: Volumetric Supervision for 3D Gaussian Segmentation
abstract: 3D Gaussian Splatting enables object-level operations on Gaussian primitives, yet existing segmentation methods are largely trained and evaluated through rendered views. This mismatch can produce accurate rendered masks from incomplete 3D selections since alpha-blended feature supervision concentrates learning on dominant contributors while leaving occluded or low-contribution Gaussians weakly supervised. We propose VODA, a plug-and-play supervision objective that exploits local depth structure to group per-pixel contributors and directly supervises all Gaussians in selected depth clusters, bypassing contribution-weighted gradient delivery. To evaluate volumetric completeness, we introduce Removal-3D, a synthetic object-removal benchmark, and the Removal Depth Error (RDE), a metric comparing predicted and ground-truth depth changes. Across four rendering-based baselines, VODA consistently improves volumetric segmentation on Removal-3D while maintaining or improving performance on LERF and ScanNet. Further analysis shows that VODA recovers lower-contribution Gaussians, while simple gradient reweighting and spatial propagation fail to reproduce comparable gains.

title: LynnReal-Hand: Unlocking World Interaction with Hand Control
abstract: Interactive video world models enable exploration through text and camera controls, yet direct object interaction requires finer control. Hands provide a natural interface, but translating continuous hand movements into coherent visual responses remains challenging because of complex hand-object dynamics and demanding real-time computation. To address these challenges, we introduce LynnReal-Hand, a hand-controlled video world model that unifies precise interaction modeling with efficient streaming generation. We curate 100K interaction clips spanning diverse real and synthetic environments and develop hand-aware supervision to improve fine-grained hand motions and object interactions. Building on this foundation, we learn a causal flow map for few-step generation and introduce region-aware score distillation that combines complementary video and image priors to refine interaction dynamics and visual appearance. To further reduce inference latency, we propose Ultra-Fast-VAE, a compact video decoder that preserves high reconstruction fidelity with substantially lower computational cost. Extensive evaluations on HandBench demonstrate superior hand-following accuracy and visual quality

title: Lost in the Hallway: Benchmarking Persistent Spatial Memory Across Revisits
abstract: Persistent spatial understanding is essential for embodied agents to operate reliably in environments they repeatedly encounter. It requires recognizing revisited places despite viewpoint changes, distinguishing them from similar-looking rooms, and updating memories as environments change. Yet existing evaluations often leave physical place identity across separated visits implicit. We introduce ReSpaceBench, a benchmark comprising 3,244 questions across 590 synthetic and real-home scenes, organized into 9 tasks spanning room association, persistent state tracking, and downstream reasoning. Controlled walkthroughs define visits by physical room entry and deliberately include same-type room distractors and cross-session object changes. Our evaluation of 32 models and 3 agentic video-understanding frameworks reveals substantial limitations: the strongest evaluated zero-shot model achieves 50.5% overall accuracy and 52.2% on a 450-question subset, compared with 90.1% for human annotators. The evaluated agentic frameworks offer no overall improvement over direct inference with the same base model. title: LoC-IN: Real-Time Localization of Cameras in Neural Rendered Prior LiDAR Maps
abstract: arXiv:2511.16349v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Accurate camera localization is crucial for robotics and Extended Reality (XR), enabling reliable navigation and alignment of virtual and real content. Existing visual methods often suffer from drift, scale ambiguity, and depend on fiducials or loop closure. This work introduces a real-time method for localizing a camera within a pre-captured, highly accurate colored LiDAR point cloud. By rendering synthetic views from this cloud, 2D-3D correspondences are established between live frames and the point cloud. A neural rendering technique narrows the domain gap between synthetic and real images, reducing occlusion and background artifacts to improve feature matching. The result is drift-free camera tracking with correct metric scale in the global LiDAR coordinate system. Two real-time variants are presented: Online Render and Match (R&M), and Prebuild and Localize (P&L). We demonstrate improved results on the ScanNet++ dataset and outperform existing SLAM pipelines.

title: EgoEMG: A Multimodal Egocentric Dataset with Bilateral EMG and Vision for Hand Pose Estimation
abstract: Hand pose estimation from egocentric video is challenging under adverse visual conditions, such as occlusion. Wrist-worn surface electromyography (sEMG) measures muscle activity without requiring visual access to the hand, offering a wearable complement to egocentric cameras. Evaluating their combined use requires synchronized physiological and visual recordings with continuous pose annotations, which existing EMG-based hand pose datasets do not jointly provide. We introduce EgoEMG, a multimodal dataset pairing bilateral wrist sEMG with egocentric video and motion-capture-derived hand poses, supplemented by external multi-view RGB-D recordings. EgoEMG contains 25.9 hours of recordings from 68 participants, covering 60 bare-hand gesture classes and interactions with 10 everyday objects. We establish EMG-only, vision-only, and fusion benchmarks with shared 22-dimensional pose targets and evaluations on unseen users, gestures, and objects. For EMG-only estimation, EMGFormer achieves the lowest overall MAE among the compared methods on EgoEMG and competitive results on EMG2Pose. Our residual fusion model combines ViT and EMGFormer features. Adding EMG reduces error for both single-fram

title: DeformMaster: An Interactive Physics-Neural World Model for Deformable Objects from Videos
abstract: World models for deformable objects should recover not only geometry and appearance, but also underlying physical dynamics, interaction grounding, and material behavior. Learning such a model from real videos is challenging because deformable linear, planar, and volumetric objects evolve under high-dimensional deformation, noisy interactions, and complex material response. The model must infer a physical state from visual observations, roll it forward under new interactions, and render the resulting dynamics with high visual fidelity. We therefore present DeformMaster, a video-derived interactive physics-neural world model that turns real interaction videos into an online interactive model of deformable objects within a unified dynamics-and-appearance framework. DeformMaster preserves structured physical rollout while using a neural residual to compensate for unmodeled effects, grounds sparse hand motion as distributed compliant actuators for hand-continuum interaction, represents material response with spatially varying constitutive experts, and drives high-fidelity 4D appearance from the predicted physical evolution. title: MACRO: Training-free Multi-plane Attention for Closeup Render Optimization
abstract: Close-up rendering, zooming into a scene well beyond any training camera, is important for virtual production and interactive 3D content, yet remains an open challenge. 3D Gaussian splatting (3DGS) enables high-fidelity, real-time novel view synthesis, but its rendering quality degrades at close range. Recent diffusion-based methods that enhance the rendering by conditioning on reference images from the training set produce significant artifacts in this setting. We analyze this failure and identify its root cause: the scale gap between the close-up and reference views. We show that the features in reference-conditioned enhancement models are not scale-invariant, causing cross-view attention to retrieve incorrect correspondences when the same content appears at different scales, and that this mismatch cannot be corrected in latent space because the VAE encoder is not scale-equivariant. Building on this analysis we introduce MACRO, Multi-plane Attention for Closeup Render Optimization, a training-free method for high-quality close-up novel view synthesis from 3DGS. title: Comparative Evaluation of an XR Pen-based Control Interface for Semi-Autonomous Mobile Robot Navigation in Service Environments
abstract: arXiv:2609.31117v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Service robots remain difficult to deploy in domestic environments, partly because fully autonomous operation is not yet reliable in unpredictable surroundings, and partly because conventional control methods remain inaccessible to novice users. Extended Reality (XR) enables operators to visualize robot information overlaid onto the real world and to interact with augmented elements. Yet, common XR control methods, such as motion controllers and hand gestures, are still perceived as unintuitive. This paper presents a control interface that uses a commercial XR pen to command a semi-autonomous mobile robot in Augmented Reality (AR): the operator points at a position in the room, selects it, and drags an augmented arrow to set the desired orientation of the robot at this destination. Two additional interfaces, based on the XR motion controllers and hand gestures, were developed within the same framework. To assess the performance and users' perception of these interfaces, and of the XR pen in particular, a study with 10 participants compared four control methods, i.e., the XR pen, the XR motion controllers, hand gestures, and

title: TetraCoder: Adaptive Tetrahedral Encoding for Neural Fields
abstract: Implicit and explicit representations of geometry are central in computer graphics applications and come with their pros and cons. With surface sampling being faster on explicit representations and spatial queries being faster on implicit representations, finding efficient conversions between them is a highly desirable property. We present TetraCoder, a single resolution hash-free adaptive tetrahedral encoding that links an explicit tetrahedral spatial encoder with an underlying implicit signed distance field (SDF). The resulting hybrid implicit-explicit space is continuous piecewise affine (CPWA) by design, allowing to obtain an exact correspondence between the implicit SDF and the explicit analytic mesh. TetraCoder's design comes with additional perks, in particular: (a) it scales better than multi-resolution encoding methods due to its single resolution optimizable grid, (b) unlike hash-based methods, it is not affected by collisions, (c) it enables fast tetrahedral ray-tracing, geometry and appearance editing, directly through its adaptive tetrahedral scaffold. We demonstrate the versatility of TetraCoder by showing an improvement over state-of-the-art methods on multiple tasks

title: GOOSELoc: A Multimodal Benchmark for Ground-to-Aerial Localization in Unstructured Off-Road Terrain
abstract: Cross-view pose estimation estimates a ground camera's geographic pose by matching onboard sensor data with geo-referenced overhead imagery. This is particularly relevant when GNSS is unreliable, for example under forest canopy or in urban canyons. Existing metric cross-view benchmarks, such as VIGOR and cross-view KITTI, are dominated by urban and road scenes with strong human-made structure without off-road terrain. We introduce GOOSELoc, a multimodal benchmark for ground-to-aerial localization in unstructured environments, including forests, fields, and rural tracks. GOOSELoc comprises 9,356 scenes recorded across all four seasons around Munich, Germany, pairing geo-referenced aerial orthophotos with surround-view RGB imagery and 3D LiDAR point clouds. Paved/unpaved labels enable analyzing the impact of terrain structure, while the seasonal recordings allow studying the appearance gap to mostly summer-captured orthophotos. To assess the transferability of existing methods, we adapt and fine-tune four state-of-the-art cross-view localization baselines on GOOSELoc. title: Agents Cannot Hand Over What They Have Not Yet Understood
abstract: Agents that work beyond a single context window, or in teams, hand their work to a successor as a short written summary. Evaluation has focused on whether an agent can solve a task, and relatively little is known about how much of what an agent has learned survives being written down. We study this in 56 interactive worlds with hidden rules, where an agent that is told nothing fails and an agent given a 300-character statement of the rules succeeds. We compare one agent that plays eight lives and keeps its whole history with a chain of eight agents that each play one life and inherit a 300-character note. All six models we test learn less in the chain: after eight generations it stands where the single agent stood after about four lives. Controlled variants of the chain decompose this handoff loss into three components: none from changing the agent, a smaller loss from compressing to 300 characters, and a larger loss from compressing repeatedly. When each note is written from the full record of earlier lives instead of from the previous note, the same 300 characters recover 70% to 82% of the loss. The loss is robust across model sizes and is not alleviated by instructing the writer

title: SynPanZ: A Synthetic Dataset to Improve Multi-Animal Pose Estimation in Chimpanzees (Pan troglodytes)
abstract: Pose estimation underpins a wide range of automated monitoring workflows in animal behaviour research. Unfortunately, endangered great apes such as chimpanzees suffer a chronic shortage of the type of hand-annotated training data that has made robust pose estimation in humans and other model organisms possible. This paper introduces SynPanZ, a synthetically generated dataset for pose estimation in great apes. Our pipeline renders multi-individual scenes from rigged, behaviourally animated chimpanzee models with randomised poses, lighting conditions, environmental contexts, and camera motion, producing animated RGB videos with per-instance 2D keypoint locations without manual labelling. To test whether synthetic augmentation improves cross-dataset generalisation, four DeepLabCut models are trained under matched settings on data sourced from DeepWild with varying real-to-synthetic augmentation ratios. Models are evaluated on ChimpACT, a visually disjoint zoo dataset. We find that augmenting the DeepWild training data with approximately three times as many synthetic frames nearly doubles instance coverage (12.34% to 22.54%) while maintaining keypoint localisation accuracy on detected

title: Detection Is Not the Finish Line: Multiscale Decoding and Constraint-Aware Global Association for Multi-Camera 3D Tracking
abstract: A query-based multi-view 3D detector can transfer well to a new calibrated camera network and still produce badly fragmented tracks: on the AI City Challenge 2026 Track 1 validation set, the frozen Sparse4D detector behind the official challenge winner splits each Person identity into a median of eight fragments, and half of the gaps between fragments exceed the horizon of a causal tracker. We show that most of the remaining headroom of such a system lies after detection. Keeping the public detector frozen, we add (i) class-wise source selection between two input scales, which recovers small and distant people from a 0.75x pass while leaving large objects at the scale the detector was trained for; (ii) a geometry-to-appearance bridge that projects every 3D box into all calibrated views, matches it to 2D person detections, and aggregates robust track-level re-identification descriptors; and (iii) constraint-aware consolidation, which combines a causal short-gap stitch with offline centroid-linkage clustering under two hard constraints, temporal exclusion and metric 3D reachability, plus class-aware long-gap stitching for rigid objects. title: Target-Free Autocalibration of Stereo PIV Camera Systems via Persistent-State Motion Representations
abstract: Stereo Particle Image Velocimetry (PIV) recovers three-component velocity fields by triangulating tracer particles observed by synchronized cameras. It requires an accurate extrinsic calibration, which is still obtained by inserting a physical target into the flow and must be repeated whenever the rig is moved. We present a target-free method that calibrates a stereo PIV rig directly from particle image sequences. Because tracer particles are visually indistinguishable, we match motion rather than appearance: building on CUT3R, each camera stream is processed by a recurrent transformer whose persistent state accumulates particle motion over time. The state is decoded into per-camera optical flow and queried by a cross-view decoder that regresses bidirectional point correspondences, from which the relative pose is recovered with a five-point RANSAC solver. We train on a new synthetic stereo PIV dataset with ground-truth poses and evaluate on standard PIV optical flow benchmarks and on 200 real rig placements. Our model achieves lower flow error than existing PIV networks, more accurate cross-view correspondences than COTR, and higher pose accuracy than the strongest detector-matcher

title: Neural Latent Gaussian Process for 3D reconstruction of Mouse Brain Lipids
abstract: We address the problem of reconstructing continuous three-dimensional lipid profiles of the mouse brain from lipid measurements acquired only on a sparse set of two-dimensional tissue sections. Using MALDI-MSI measurements from coronal sections of two densely sampled and six sparsely sampled mouse brains, registered to the Allen Mouse Brain Common Coordinate Framework (CCF), we seek to interpolate the measured hundreds of lipid profiles across the unobserved voxels of the reference brain. We introduce a Neural Latent-Space Gaussian Process (LGP) architecture for this task and critically evaluate its ability to reconstruct spatial lipid distributions, using held-out mouse brain sections to assess generalization. We propose a Gaussian Process prior for the distribution of low-dimensional lipid profiles across the mouse brain (with Mat\'ern or a Riemann manifold kernel). This allows us to encode 3D coordinates in a small number of latent 3D volumes that are then mapped to particular lipids using a multilayer perceptron (MLP). title: ST-Dist: Distilling Spatial Transcriptomics Predictions into Interpretable Gene Axes for Distant Metastasis Prediction
abstract: Distant metastasis at diagnosis determines the treatment of prostate cancer, but predicting it from routine biopsy slides is challenging as the signs of metastasis are not clearly localized and are more subtle than in standard tumor detection and subtyping tasks. Multiple instance learning (MIL) on pathology foundation-model features has become the standard approach when labeled data are abundant, but such models remain hard to interpret. Distant metastasis is further challenging, because confirming the label requires clinical follow-up beyond the routine H&E slides. To this end, we propose ST-Dist, which distills the gene expression predicted by a spatial transcriptomics (ST) model into a linear head mapping each tile's foundation-model features onto named gene axes. The slide's projections along these interpretable gene axes are then used for distant metastasis prediction with a simple logistic regression. On 497 prostate needle biopsies (205 patients), ST-Dist reaches an AUROC of 91.37%, above nine MIL baselines. title: Angel: Anchor-Structured Neural Gaussians for Explicit Fetal Diffusion MRI Slice-to-Volume Reconstruction with Cross-Subject Learning
abstract: Diffusion magnetic resonance imaging (dMRI) provides a noninvasive view of developing tissue microstructure and white matter tracts in the fetal brain. During acquisition, however, fetal motion disrupts spatial correspondence between slices, diffusion encoding directions and signal intensities. We introduce ANGEL, an anchor-structured neural Gaussian framework for accurate slice-to-volume reconstruction (SVR) of fetal dMRI, that simultaneously estimates diffusion signal, fetal motion and intensity artefacts. Unlike standard explicit Gaussian representation, ANGEL is designed to prevent absorption of noise and artefacts into the reconstructed dMRI by learning a compact representation of spatio-angular signal via a shared decoder that predicts 3D Gaussians across anchors and subjects. The individual anatomical variability is compactly represented through subject-specific anchors. Experiments on simulated neonatal and in vivo fetal data show significant improvement of dMRI reconstruction in both spatial and angular domains, in comparison to explicit Gaussian representation, implicit neural representation as well as classical methods.

title: Third-Place Solution for the UCF UrbanTwin V2X-Real Track at ECCV 2026: Synthetic Point Cloud Generation and Sim-to-Real 3D Object Detection
abstract: This report presents a complete technical solution for the UrbanTwin V2X-Real Sim2Real LiDAR Challenge, covering both synthetic point cloud generation and 3D object detection. For data generation, we adopt per-axis quantile calibration. Public V2X-Real training data are used to construct the real reference distribution, and independent one-dimensional quantile mappings are estimated for the x, y, and z axes of the base synthetic point clouds. The calibrated point clouds are then resampled using a fixed random seed and clipped to the valid spatial range, producing 50 frames with 2,000 float32 XYZ points per frame. For detection, we use a two-stage Voxel R-CNN (VoxelRCNN) detector trained with RangeLDM-enhanced synthetic point-cloud data, point clouds downsampled to 50k points per frame, and reconstructed pedestrian data. Training is performed on four NVIDIA GeForce RTX 4090 GPUs with a global batch size of 16 for 40 epochs. Final testing uses direct single-model inference with the original VoxelRCNN model. On the official evaluation server, the normalized Realism score is 0.7905 and the normalized Detection score is 0.5583, with mAP@0.5 of 0.3908, BEV mAP@0.5 of 0.4219, and mAP@0.7

title: UnSPAD: Uncertainty-aware Single Photon Burst Photography
abstract: We introduce UnSPAD, an uncertainty-aware burst photography framework capable of fusing and denoising arbitrarily long sequences of binary single photon avalanche diode (SPAD) measurements. Unlike prior methods that require fixed burst lengths or rely on powerful generative priors, UnSPAD combines learned motion estimation with uncertainty-informed measurement fusion and denoising to produce temporally consistent, hallucination-free reconstructions. UnSPAD first forms an initial scene estimate by averaging flow-aligned binary frames. UnSPAD then uses per-pixel uncertainty maps to perform uncertainty-aware denoising; the denoiser is informed about which regions accumulated the fewest observations (and thus contain the most relative shot noise) due to motion, occlusion, or alignment errors. This two-step reconstruction pipeline helps mitigate hallucinations---outside of the structure implicitly introduced by the flow estimates, the initial scenes estimates are entirely prior-free. title: Correcting Persistent Failures in Point-Cloud Grasping Policies using Human Demonstrations in Virtual Reality
abstract: Robots in homes, warehouses and farms must pick up objects they have never seen, usually without a 3D model or a category label. A grasping policy that works directly on the point cloud from a depth sensor needs only the geometry the robot observes, so it applies to any new object. Offline grasp generators such as Contact-GraspNet work this way, but they rank grasps by learned plausibility rather than by whether the grasp actually lifts the object. Reinforcement learning (RL) can optimize for that directly and make a point-cloud grasping policy much better on average, yet it leaves specific grasps persistently unsolved. We present a human-in-the-loop failure loop that targets those grasps: situations an RL policy keeps failing are mined automatically, sent to a virtual-reality application where a person picks the object up with their own hands, and returned to training as two grasp points. The person contributes only where to grasp; the robot chooses its own approach. In simulation, RL raises success on unseen objects from 55% with Contact-GraspNet to 83%. title: TMA: Sim-to-Real Forceful Humanoid Manipulation via Tactile-Driven Motor Adaptation
abstract: Recent humanoid loco-manipulation in articulated environments has largely focused on geometry-dominant interactions, where success is primarily determined by geometric alignment and motion execution. In contrast, forceful multi-finger manipulation requires the robot to adapt to real-world uncertainties in contact and interaction dynamics. We present Tactile-Driven Motor Adaptation (TMA) and an integrated whole-body system for zero-shot sim-to-real forceful humanoid manipulation, and study round-doorknob opening as a challenging benchmark requiring stable multi-finger frictional grasping, sufficient torque generation without slip, force-regulated pushing, and whole-body stability. TMA structures policy learning around interactions observable through tactile feedback, uses cone geometry as an inductive bias for multi-finger contact representation, and adapts motor behavior online from tactile history. An upper-body manipulation policy is trained alongside a pretrained general locomotion controller to coordinate dexterous interaction and whole-body stabilization. title: Aspirational Identities: How VTubing Affords New Modes of Digital Embodiment
abstract: VTubing, short for "Virtual YouTubing", is a modality of streaming where a CGI avatar is used in place of the streamer's analog face and body. As VTubing has become increasingly popular, especially for queer and trans streamers of color, it is worth studying as a way for streamers to express identities that they hope to embody, which we call "aspirational identities". In this workshop submission, we draw on preliminary findings from qualitative research to argue that VTubing is a potent object of study for understanding digital embodiment and the performance of identity online, especially for questions of race, gender, sexuality, and disability.

title: Midsagittal Corpus Callosum Parameterization: A Framework for Spatially Detailed Diffusion MR Imaging Analysis
abstract: The corpus callosum (CC) is the largest white matter structure in the human brain and plays a central role in interhemispheric communication. Diffusion MR imaging is widely used to investigate microstructural organization, but commonly used analysis approaches have important limitations. Voxel-based methods rely heavily on accurate inter-subject registration and smoothing choices, tract-based spatial statistics (TBSS) restricts the analysis to a narrow white matter skeleton, and parcellation approaches reduce spatial detail by averaging diffusion measures over relatively large regions. In this work, we introduce a parameterization framework for the analysis of the midsagittal CC that resamples the structure using a standardized grid of points, establishing a geometric correspondence across individuals without explicit inter-subject registration. In a test-retest dataset, the method provided stable measurements while covering most of the midsagittal CC, and sensitivity analyses showed that results in the central CC changed little under perturbations of the input CC mask, whereas peripheral regions were more sensitive. title: ANCHOR: A Port-Hamiltonian Model for Forecasting Team Dynamics in Human-in-the-Loop Systems
abstract: Cyber-physical-human systems close a loop around people by sensing human behavior, predict it and act on it. Human teams are a natural target, because collaboration breaks down in ways that a timely prompt could prevent. Collaborative mixed reality makes this loop practical, since each headset senses who speaks, where its wearer looks and who stands together, and it can deliver a light prompt. In this loop, the headsets are sensors, the prompts are actuators and the team is the plant. Closing the loop needs a plant model that is small enough to learn from few teams, safe to iterate and readable by a designer. We propose ANCHOR, which models a team as a ball in an energy bowl. The bottom of the bowl is where the team rests, and it is set by the team's recent behavior, its own history and other teams. Formally, ANCHOR is a switched port-Hamiltonian system with 52 parameters, and each part stands for a testable claim from team psychology. Because of this structure, for any fitted parameters, a forecast moves away from rest only when task progress or a prompt pushes it, and prompts of bounded size that are spaced in time move it a bounded distance. title: Calibrating the Uncertainty of Self-Supervised Monocular Depth without Labels
abstract: Self-supervised monocular depth networks can predict a per-pixel uncertainty, which is mainly evaluated by how well it ranks pixels according to their error. Such metrics are insensitive to the magnitude of the uncertainty, so an uncertainty half as large as the actual error obtains the same score. In this paper, we investigate whether the predicted uncertainty is as large as the depth error, both on average (scale) and across confident and uncertain, near and far pixels (shape). On KITTI, the scale is miscalibrated for every uncertainty estimate we evaluate, and the error of MonoProb is nearly twice its predicted uncertainty. We propose MonoCal, which corrects both the scale and the shape without ground-truth depth. Scale calibration multiplies the uncertainty by a single constant measured from stereo pairs, requiring no retraining, and this constant closely matches the one fitted with ground truth. Since a constant cannot change the shape, we further retrain the uncertainty to predict where the depth of the network disagrees with that of a second self-supervised network. Experiments on KITTI show that MonoCal achieves better calibration across uncertainty levels and depth ranges

title: Ego2Sim2Humanoid: Agentic Real-to-Sim for Learning Loco-Manipulation VLAs without Robot Demonstrations
abstract: Imitation learning for visuomotor policies typically relies on teleoperated robot demonstrations, which are costly because every episode requires a trained operator controlling a physical robot in real time through teleoperation interfaces and wearable body-tracking hardware. Egocentric glasses capture human demonstrations without a robot or handheld grippers, yet they track only the head and in-view human hands, and directly copying human motion to a robot with different stature, arm reach and hand morphology fails to produce feasible contacts. \method{} converts egocentric glasses recordings into physically verified robot training trajectories. An agentic real-to-sim stage reconstructs collision and textured visual assets from the recorded RGB-D and head streams, completes unseen surfaces when needed, and predicts target contact bands on the manipulated objects. During motion adaptation, a grasp planner turns each contact band into a feasible robot wrist pose and finger closure, bilevel stance optimization plans collision-free standing postures that keep hand targets reachable, and a whole-body motion generator synthesizes lower-body locomotion and out-of-view arm motion. title: Continuous Lower-Limb Joint-Angle Estimation from sEMG and IMU: The Conditional Value of Cross-Activity and Cross-Subject Data under Update-Matched Controls
abstract: Intent-driven exoskeleton control needs a continuous, causal estimate of the wearer's joint kinematics and an answer to a second question: whose data should train the estimator for a new user? Borrowing the user's recordings of other activities, or other users' recordings of the same activity, is usually evaluated as "more data" versus "less data," which confounds the information a source carries with the optimizer updates it adds and hides negative transfer behind averages. We separate these effects for hip, knee, and ankle angle estimation from high-density sEMG and an IMU across six locomotion activities on all ten participants of a public dataset. A compact residual causal TCN-GRU decoder is frozen, and an update-matched replay control prices every added source against the same number of updates on the user's own data. title: Distributed Shaping of Robot Swarms Through Spatial Moments of Arbitrary Order
abstract: This paper shapes a swarm into a target pattern, such as a figure taken from an image, by controlling its spatial moments. The image is sampled into a reference configuration whose centroid and covariance set the position and principal spreads of the formation, while its higher-order moments, expressed in covariance-normalized (whitened) coordinates, encode the remaining shape. In contrast with geometric formation control, which prescribes distances, bearings, or relative positions between specific agents, this specification concerns the swarm as a whole and assigns no agent to a particular place. The key mechanism is orthogonalization in the swarm's own empirical inner product: projecting negative-gradient velocities onto the complement of low-degree polynomials sampled at the agents makes every higher-order correction preserve all lower-order moments exactly. The resulting hierarchical controller has lower triangular error dynamics and converges locally exponentially for any positive gains, so orders can be added without undoing those already achieved. title: Residual Reinforcement Learning for Visual Servo Control with Zero-Shot Sim-to-Real Transfer
abstract: We address tracking a moving object on a conveyor with a Franka Emika Panda robot arm, despite an imprecise digital twin, measurement errors, and noise. Our novel approach augments a loop-shaped inverse-Jacobian PI controller with a residual policy learned via Soft Actor-Critic in the digital twin. A delay-compensated Kalman filter fuses out-of-sequence camera measurements to provide latency-aware moving target position estimates. We compare the achieved performance to a performance bound for a class of model-based controllers derived from a frequency-domain sensitivity analysis, quantifying the minimum achievable error imposed by uncertain kinematic model mismatch. Simulation and hardware experiments indicate that our residual policy drives tracking error below the bound. Across conveyor speeds (27.9-41.8 mm/s), our method reduces mean tracking errors from 1.1-1.4 mm (baseline inverse-Jacobian PI) to 0.3-0.7 mm. These results show that learning residual corrections in a limited-fidelity simulator, combined with delay compensation, can substantially improve model-based control under modeling and measurement uncertainties while maintaining reliable sim-to-real transfer.

title: AcousticBEV: Acoustic BEV Object Localization for Intelligent Vehicles
abstract: Modern autonomous driving and driver assistance systems rely predominantly on cameras, radars and LiDARs for environmental perception. However, these modalities face different environmental limitations, including poor illumination for cameras and adverse weather for LiDAR. Acoustic sensing, particularly using microphone arrays, could provide complementary perception capabilities for autonomous driving, but has remained largely underexplored. In this work, we design a horizontally arranged microphone array that functions as the "ears" of a vehicle, enabling localization of nearby moving vehicles in a bird's-eye view (BEV) representation that captures both their relative direction and distance. Using this array, we collect a real-world driving dataset, AcousticScenes, which contains 2,117 static and 2,863 dynamic samples with synchronized spatial acoustic signals, LiDAR point clouds and 3D bounding box annotations. Building on this dataset, we propose AcousticBEV, a learning-based method for acoustic BEV object localization, which estimates the center locations of moving traffic participants in BEV from the microphone-array signals, conditioned on the ego vehicle's own speed. title: Depth-Aware Path Planning and Collision Avoidance for Robotic Nursing Assistants Using Real-Time 3D Vision
abstract: This paper presents a depth-aware path planning and collision avoidance framework for the safe navigation of robotic nursing assistants in cluttered environments with low-height obstacles. Conventional LiDAR-based navigation systems, while accurate for mapping and localization, fail to detect transparent or low-height obstacles, whereas vision-based systems are prone to noise and occlusion. The proposed framework integrates RGB-D depth sensing, rule-based obstacle avoidance, and the NavfnROS global path planner to drive the robot from an initial point to a goal point. The proposed approach is implemented on the Husky A200 robot, equipped with a Kinova Gen3 arm, to form a complete setup for a robotic nursing assistant. This system features a multi-layer architecture for global planning, perception fusion, and real-time control in the ROS-Gazebo environment. Experimental evaluations in a simulated cluttered environment demonstrate up to 40\% higher success rate and 35\% improvement in minimum clearance compared with single-sensor baselines. Furthermore, real-world experimental results validate the proposed approach as a computationally efficient and safety-aware navigation solution f

title: Sharp First-Hit Identification from Finite Depth Samples
abstract: Which depths in a new camera view are determined by finitely many source-depth measurements? Pointwise uncertainty bounds do not answer this question: unobserved geometry between samples can change which surface is encountered first. We study a bounded Lipschitz class of continuous source inverse-depth fields with interval observations and known camera pose. Building on classical Lipschitz envelopes, we characterize the exact set of attainable first-hit depths and construct a globally admissible scene for every value in that set. The set can be disconnected. We also give a necessary and sufficient test for several proposed depths to be first hits of one shared scene. An epipolar reduction uses scalar cone inequalities without enumerating surfaces. In a rectified model with source spacing $h$, interval half-width $\varepsilon$, baseline $b$, and slope bound $L$, we prove a sharp worst-case inverse-depth diameter of $\max\{Lh+2\varepsilon,2\varepsilon/(1-bL)\}$ when $bL<1$, subject to sufficient depth and domain range for attainment. title: Learning Spatially Aware Audio-Visual Features from Videos with Mono Audio
abstract: Comprehensive audio-visual perception requires both semantic and spatial reasoning. Existing spatial models suffer from poor generalization due to data scarcity, while semantic-only models fail to capture spatial characteristics completely. We introduce a model capable of jointly reasoning over binaural audio and vision on semantic and spatial tasks with improved generalization. To overcome the shortage in real-world data, we develop an automatic pipeline that localizes the sound source in a video, estimates its relative 3D trajectory, and renders binaural audio. We then use this to spatialize VGGSound, allowing us to train at a much larger scale. We demonstrate improved performance and generalization on spatial reasoning tasks while still remaining competitive on semantic tasks compared to semantic-only models.

title: Well-Log Reconstruction with Pre-trained Geological Knowledge: A Knowledge-Conditioned Large-Language-Model Generative Agent
abstract: Missing well-log intervals make subsurface reconstruction ill-posed. Existing numerical regression models lack geological prior knowledge to constrain ambiguous inverse mappings. We propose GeoLog-Agent, a knowledge-conditioned generative agent using pre-trained large language models (LLMs) as a source of geological priors. A universal Geo-Harness translates LLM stratigraphic reasoning into formation-anchored petrophysical trajectories, feature-wise linear modulation, and conditional adversarial constraints. On the Norwegian North Sea benchmark, GeoLog-Agent achieves a mean $R^2$ of 0.9307 and a peak $R^2$ of 0.9713. It exceeds the nine-baseline average $R^2$ of 0.8387 by 0.0920, with a 30.97% average RMSE reduction, and exceeds the strongest baseline by 0.0274--0.0498 in $R^2$, with 16.25%--24.05% lower RMSE. Ablations confirm the effectiveness and synergy of geological prior reasoning, multi-scale dilated generation, and conditional adversarial modules. Transferring the coupling mechanism to six conventional deep learning models improves their $R^2$ by 0.0162--0.0789 with cross-well stability. These results demonstrate how foundation-model domain reasoning can constrain deep gene

title: Floorplan-Context-Aware Cross-Environment Human Activity Recognition from mmWave Radar Point Clouds
abstract: Human activity recognition (HAR) models based on mmWave radar point clouds and trained in controlled open spaces often experience performance degradation when deployed in furnished rooms. We propose a Floorplan-Context-Aware (FCA) HAR enhancement method that augments the input with subject-furniture relative position information to improve cross-environment performance. Because existing mmWave point-cloud datasets lack registered floorplans, we introduce a pseudo-landmark augmentation strategy for training the FCA model. In cross-environment evaluation on the mm-ADL-Home dataset, FCA achieves 77.70% accuracy and 65.49% macro-F1, improving upon the point-cloud-only direct-transfer baseline by 10.73 and 10.05 percentage points, respectively, and exceeding the strongest evaluated adaptation baseline by 7.37 and 6.27 percentage points. At deployment, FCA requires only a one-time registration of furniture landmarks, with no target-domain activity annotations or model weight updates.

title: Real-Time Air Pollution Monitoring and Tracking via Adaptive Density-Driven Multi-UAV Coordination
abstract: Accurate and timely air pollution monitoring and tracking are critical for protecting public health and supporting effective environmental management. This paper presents an adaptive Density-Driven Control (D$^2$C) framework for coordinating multiple unmanned aerial vehicles (UAVs) to track and map dynamically evolving pollutant distributions. The proposed framework extends the D$^2$C strategy to guide UAV trajectories based on predictive pollutant propagation and dynamically updated reference densities. A sensor-driven surrogate plume update mechanism is employed, in which reference samples are propagated using locally sensed concentration gradients and wind estimates through gradient attraction, wind advection, inter-sample repulsion, and stochastic diffusion, enabling UAVs to maintain an accurate spatio-temporal representation of the pollution field. The framework utilizes a coordinated structure where individual UAVs share their local measurements with a central coordinator to maintain a unified set of reference samples, facilitating systematic target allocation and trajectory planning. title: Sim-to-Real Room-Mediated Object-Goal Navigation with ROS 2 and Nav2
abstract: Although object-goal navigation (ObjectNav) approaches are usually evaluated in simulation, which offers scale and repeatable environments, real-world deployments are rarely examined beyond feasibility demonstrations. This paper presents the deployment of Room-Mediated Co-occurrence, an ObjectNav policy that reasons over Room Probability Vectors (RPVs), on two robotic platforms (Boston Dynamics Spot and Clearpath Robotics TurtleBot 4) through a robot-agnostic ROS 2 bridge. We study how these semantic priors generalise to physical environments and describe the adaptations required to transfer RPV from simulation to hardware, covering sensing, localisation, and the action interface. Across 66 trials on Spot, searching for 11 object categories from two starting positions in a university postgraduate research facility, RPV achieves a raw Success Rate (SR) of 0.455. Our analysis identifies undetected glass walls, entry into off-limits areas, limited usable depth range, target size, and mismatch between the room lexicon and physical layout as plausible contributors to the 8.4 percentage-point gap between the real-world SR and the reported simulated SR of 0.539.
